They hated him and could not speak to him in a peaceful manner. For the writer of the book has made an exact enumeration of those who came from Esau. Who came from whom and where each of them settled and what rule they received, the scripture has taught us. Nothing noble or worthy of memory was done. The word attends to the named ones, but it is directed towards Joseph as if towards a divine one. And it makes a brilliant story of those from the blood of Jacob. Joseph, the youngest of the others, was seventeen years old and not idle in pastoral work. He was involved with his other brothers in equal endeavors, not having valued the laziness most dear to those in youth. Not renouncing the early care of life, nor having loved to be idle, as he was still in his youth. But like an old man, already having come into a good state of mind and having a well-established intellect. Using mature speech and foreshadowing the beauty of future glory, he was reasonably admired by his blessed and loving father, and he was exceptionally worthy of love and care. For he was, it says, a son of his old age. And what is this? The word is concerned with the dispositions in us. For the loving affections towards children of those who have given birth are equal in every way and in no way diminished.

Nature often overpowers and coerces the mind, yielding a little to the weaker ones, persuading them, as they are in need of frugality, of the previous ones; otherwise, when many have been born, it somehow ends, and the excess of love is reserved for the last one, the affection for the preceding ones, as it somehow seizes the one with them; for human mind is fond of novelty, and does not reject the abundance of those who have already gone, but is greatly changed by those who are not yet present or have just been acquired, and receives a more intense desire for them; Jacob loved Joseph more than the others because he was his old age son; it is known that although he had previously married Leah in Haran, he loved Rachel, who bore Joseph, and died giving birth to Benjamin; we say that both were old age sons; Joseph's natural disposition was not equal to everyone; the old man showed it to be diverse, as if it had been inclined towards him; he was probably reasoning that he would be illustrious and famous; and the one who was not contemptuous of the leaps of youth, when he became a mature man, how would he not become…
pass_b_english: The brothers of Joseph hated him and were unable to speak to him in a peaceful manner.

The writer of the book of Genesis has made an exact enumeration of those who came from Esau, including their descendants and the places where they settled, as well as the rule they received, which the scripture has taught us.
However, the scripture does not record any notable or memorable deeds of these people.
Instead, it focuses on the story of Joseph, who was the youngest of his brothers and yet showed remarkable maturity and wisdom beyond his years.
Joseph was seventeen years old and was already involved in pastoral work, taking care of his father's flocks, and he was not idle, but rather worked hard and was responsible.
His father, Jacob, loved him dearly and saw in him a son of his old age, as it says, 'a son of his old age' (Genesis 37:3).
The word of God is concerned with the dispositions in us, and how we respond to those who are younger or older than us.
Human nature has a tendency to overpower and coerce the mind, often leading to a slight concession to the weaker ones, as they are in need of frugality.
This can be seen in the way that affection is distributed among children, with the excess of love being reserved for the last one.

The human mind is fond of novelty, and this is evident in the way that it does not reject the abundance of those who have already gone, but is greatly changed by those who are not yet present or have just been acquired.
This phenomenon can be observed in the story of Jacob, who loved Joseph more than his other sons because he was his old age son.
Despite having previously married Leah in Haran, Jacob's love for Rachel, who bore Joseph, was evident, and he was deeply affected by her death in childbirth, when she gave birth to Benjamin.
Joseph's natural disposition was not equal to everyone, and the old man showed it to be diverse, as if it had been inclined towards him.

As Joseph grew into a mature man, his character and abilities became increasingly evident, and it is likely that he would become a great and famous person, probably reasoning that he would be illustrious and famous.

Νεώτατος μὲν οὖν τῶν ἄλλων ὁ Ἰωσὴφ (ἑπτακαίδεκα γὰρ ἦν ἐτῶν), ἱδρῶτός γε μὴν οὐκ ἠμέλει ποιμενικοῦ· τοῖς δὲ ἄλλοις ἀδελφοῖς ἀναμὶξ τῶν ἴσων ἥπτετο σπουδασμάτων, οὐ τὴν τοῖς ἐν ἥβῃ θυμηρεστάτην καὶ ἀεί πως προσφιλῆ ῥᾳστώνην τετιμηκώς· οὐ τὴν πρόωρον τοῦ βίου φροντίδα παραιτούμενος, οὐδὲ τὸ ἀνεῖσθαι μᾶλλον ἠγαπηκὼς, ἅτε δὴ καὶ ἐν μειρακίοις ἔτι τελῶν· ἀλλ' οἷα πρεσβύτης, ἐν εὐδίᾳ μὲν ἤδη λογισμῶν γεγονὼς, καὶ τὸν νοῦν ἔχων εὖ βεβηκότα· πολιῷ τε τῷ λόγῳ χρώμενος, καὶ τῆς ἐσομένης λαμπρότητος προαναφαίνων τὸ κάλλος, ἐθαυ 69.288 μάζετο μὲν εἰκότως παρά γε τῷ μακαρίῳ καὶ φιλοστόργῳ πατρὶ, ἀγάπης τε καὶ φειδοῦς διαφερόντως ἠξιοῦτο. Αἱ μὲν γὰρ ἐπὶ παισὶ τῶν γεγεννηκότων φιλοστοργίαι, ἴσαι τε εἰς ἅπαν παρά γέ τισι, καὶ κατ' οὐδένα τρόπον ἐν μείοσι.
